definition: Liabilities arising from borrowed funds that must be repaid.
example: Loans payable are classified as non-current liabilities.

definition: Loans in breach of their terms and repayable on demand.
example: Loans payable in default are classified as current liabilities.

definition: Benefits payable beyond twelve months.
example: Long-term employee benefits include long-service leave.

definition: An investment intended to be held for more than one year, not expected to be converted into cash in the short term.
example: Long-term investments are presented separately from current assets in the statement of financial position.

definition: Assessing the substance behind a structure.
example: A look through approach assesses the underlying assets.

definition: Basing treatment on underlying substance rather than legal form.
example: The look through approach is used for financial conglomerates.

definition: An event that causes an actual credit loss.
example: A loss event was identified on the defaulted loan.

definition: The event in which a parent no longer has control over a former subsidiary.
example: The loss of control triggered the derecognition of the subsidiary's assets and liabilities.

definition: The net loss attributable to each ordinary share.
example: The entity reported a loss per share for the period.

definition: A test to determine whether an insurance contract is onerous.
example: A loss recognition test is performed for each insurance portfolio.

definition: An agreement to share losses between parties.
example: Under the loss sharing arrangement, losses are borne proportionately.

definition: Decreases in economic benefits.
example: Losses are recognised in profit or loss.

definition: A parent entity that is itself a subsidiary of another parent higher up the group structure.
example: The lower level parent prepares consolidated financial statements for its own group within the wider structure.

definition: Ownership of more than half the voting rights.
example: Majority interest gives the parent control.

term: Managed on a contractual yield basis
definition: Assets managed to achieve returns set by contract.
example: The portfolio is managed on a contractual yield basis.

definition: The people responsible for directing and controlling an entity.
example: Management is responsible for preparing the financial statements.

definition: An approach that bases segment reporting on the information used internally by management.
example: Under the management approach, segments were reported as reviewed by the chief operating decision maker.

definition: Narrative explanation of financial results accompanying the statements.
example: The management commentary explains key performance drivers.

definition: Management's stated plans for holding or disposing of an asset.
example: The classification depended on management intentions.

definition: The difference between revenue and cost of sales.
example: The gross margin improved following cost reductions.

definition: A condition related to market prices.
example: A market condition affects the fair value of a share option.

definition: The price at which an asset or liability could be bought or sold in an active market.
example: The market price of the listed shares was used to determine their fair value.

definition: The prevailing interest rate in the market.
example: The loan was granted at the market rate of interest.

definition: Risk of loss from market price movements.
example: Market risk arises from commodity price fluctuations.

definition: The price at which an asset could be traded in the market.
example: The market value of the land rose sharply.

definition: Describes an asset that can be readily bought or sold in a market.
example: The marketable securities were measured at fair value at the reporting date.

definition: Intangible assets used in marketing, such as trademarks and brand names.
example: Marketing-related intangible assets include trademarks and internet domains.

definition: Intellectual property rights protecting semiconductor chip designs.
example: Mask works are recognised as intangible assets.

definition: An agreement allowing offsetting of multiple contracts on default.
example: A master netting arrangement allows offset on default.

definition: Recognising expenses with the related revenue.
example: Matching of costs with revenues recognises expenses in the same period.

definition: Information is material if omitting, misstating or obscuring it could influence the decisions that users make.
example: The omission of the disclosure was not material to the users of the financial statements.

definition: Adjustments significant enough to matter.
example: Material adjustments were made to the prior period figures.

definition: Errors significant enough to affect users' decisions.
example: Material errors in prior statements were corrected retrospectively.

definition: Failures to include information significant enough to affect decisions.
example: Material omissions in the notes led to a restatement.

definition: The threshold at which information could influence the economic decisions of users of financial statements.
example: The omission was not considered material to the financial statements as a whole.

definition: Presenting information across two dimensions in a grid format.
example: The matrix presentation discloses risk by type and by category.

definition: An organisational structure where staff report to more than one manager.
example: The group operates in a matrix form of organisation.

definition: The date an instrument becomes due for settlement.
example: The bond's maturity is ten years from issue.

definition: The amount payable at maturity.
example: The bond was redeemed at its maturity value.

term: Measured at fair value through other comprehensive income
definition: A measurement category for financial assets whose fair value changes are recognised in other comprehensive income rather than profit or loss.
example: The debt instrument is measured at fair value through other comprehensive income because it is held within a business model of hold to collect and sell.

definition: Determining the monetary amount of an item.
example: Measurement of the provision used the best estimate.

definition: Methods used to determine amounts in financial statements.
example: The standard lists several measurement bases.

definition: The date at which an asset or liability is measured.
example: The measurement date for the plan assets was year end.

definition: The determination of the amount of change in an item that must be recognised or disclosed.
example: The measurement of change in the fair value of the liability was recognised in profit or loss.

definition: An accounting mismatch between related assets and liabilities.
example: The derivative was held to remove a measurement or recognition inconsistency.

definition: Calculating income tax for interim periods using the estimated annual effective rate.
example: Measuring interim income tax expense requires an estimated annual rate.

definition: Fees paid to join or remain in an organisation.
example: Membership fees are recognised as revenue over the membership period.

definition: Equity held by members of a co-operative.
example: Members' shares may be classified as equity or liability.

term: Members’ Shares in Co-operative Entities and Similar Instruments
definition: An interpretation addressing whether members' shares in co-operative entities should be classified as liabilities or equity.
example: The interpretation on members' shares in co-operative entities determines when such shares are classified as equity.

definition: Goods held for resale.
example: Merchandise is reported within inventory.

definition: Combination of two entities into one.
example: The merger created the largest bank in the region.

definition: The approach used to recognise and measure transactions.
example: The company changed its method of accounting for leases.

definition: The price midway between the bid price and the asking price of a financial instrument.
example: The shares were measured using the mid-market price at the reporting date.

definition: Extracted natural resources and products derived from them.
example: Inventory of minerals and mineral products is measured at net realizable value.

definition: Required contributions set by law or regulation to fund a plan.
example: The entity paid minimum funding contributions to the pension plan.

definition: A legal minimum contribution required for a benefit plan.
example: The minimum funding requirement increased the plan liability.

definition: Payments required over the lease term.
example: Minimum lease payments are discounted in lease accounting.

definition: The portion of equity in a subsidiary not attributable, directly or indirectly, to the parent entity.
example: Minority interest is presented within equity in the consolidated statement of financial position.

definition: A mismatch between assets and liabilities.
example: The mismatch between maturities creates risk.

definition: Difference between reported and required amounts.
example: The auditor identified a misstatement in revenue.

definition: An instrument or action that reduces risk exposure.
example: The derivative served as a mitigating device for currency risk.

definition: An accounting approach under which different measurement bases are applied to different items.
example: The standard uses a mixed attribute approach, measuring some assets at cost and others at fair value.

definition: An asset representing money or a claim to fixed amounts of money.
example: Cash and trade receivables are monetary assets.

definition: Units of currency held and assets and liabilities to be received or paid in fixed amounts.
example: Monetary items are translated at the closing exchange rate.

term: Monetary items (monetary assets; monetary financial assets and financial liabilities; monetary financial instruments)
definition: Assets and liabilities to be received or paid in fixed money units.
example: Monetary items are retranslated at the closing rate.

definition: Watching adherence to rules or covenants.
example: The entity monitors compliance with loan covenants.

definition: The risk that actual mortality rates differ from those expected, affecting the measurement of insurance or benefit obligations.
example: The insurer's mortality risk was assessed using recent actuarial tables.

definition: Benefit plans shared by several employers.
example: Multi-employer plans pool the assets of several employers.

term: Multi-employer plans (for an employee benefit plan)
definition: Plan pooling contributions from several unrelated employers.
example: Multi-employer plans spread risk across participating employers.

definition: Several separate contracts entered into at or near the same time.
example: The multiple arrangements were assessed as a single transaction.

definition: Two or more embedded derivatives contained in a single host contract.
example: When a contract contains multiple embedded derivatives, they may be treated as a single compound derivative.

definition: An entity owned and controlled by its members for mutual benefit.
example: The mutual cooperative entity distributes surpluses among its members.

definition: An entity whose owners receive dividends or returns rather than equity shares.
example: A mutual entity provides its members with membership rights.

definition: A pooled investment vehicle owned by its investors.
example: Units in the mutual fund are measured at fair value.

definition: An insurer owned by its policyholders.
example: A mutual insurance company is owned by its policyholders.

definition: Local legal or regulatory requirements that an entity must comply with in addition to international standards.
example: Where national requirements differ from IFRSs, the entity discloses the nature of the differences.

definition: Presenting expenses by their nature.
example: The nature of expense method groups expenses by type.

definition: Gain when acquisition cost is below fair value acquired.
example: The bargain purchase produced negative goodwill.

definition: A transferable financial instrument that can be endorsed to another party.
example: The negotiable paper was endorsed to the bank.

definition: The amount by which total assets exceed total liabilities, equivalent to equity.
example: Net assets increased following the profitable year.

definition: Plan assets less liabilities available to pay employee benefits.
example: Net assets available for benefits grew over the reporting period.

definition: Presentation of assets and liabilities at their net amount.
example: The liability was settled on a net basis.

definition: An option settled in cash equal to the net gain.
example: The net cash-settled option is classified as a liability.

definition: Proceeds from disposal less disposal costs.
example: Net disposal proceeds reduce the gain or loss on disposal.

definition: The net amount of gains and losses arising from translating foreign currency amounts at different exchange rates.
example: Net exchange differences are recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in a separate component of equity.

definition: Identifiable assets less liabilities acquired.
example: Goodwill is the excess of consideration over net identifiable assets.

definition: Profit remaining after all expenses and taxes.
example: Net income increased by twelve percent this year.

definition: A hedge of currency exposure in a net investment abroad.
example: The group used a net investment hedge for its overseas subsidiary.

term: Net investment in a foreign entity
definition: The amount of the reporting entity's interest in the net assets of a foreign operation.
example: The intercompany loan formed part of the net investment in a foreign entity.

term: Net investment in a foreign operation
definition: The reporting entity's net share of a foreign operation's net assets.
example: Exchange differences on a net investment in a foreign operation go to equity.

definition: The gross investment in a lease discounted at the implicit interest rate.
example: The net investment in a lease equals gross investment less unearned finance income.

definition: Total expenses exceeding total income for a period.
example: The entity reported a net loss for the year.

definition: The difference between monetary assets and liabilities.
example: The net monetary position gives rise to a gain in inflation.

definition: The difference between the total assets and total liabilities of a given exposure or category.
example: The entity's net position in foreign currency was disclosed in the risk management note.

definition: Profit after all expenses and taxes.
example: Net profit for the year increased by ten percent.

term: Net profit or loss [for the period]
definition: Bottom-line result of the reporting period.
example: Net profit or loss is presented on the income statement.

term: Net Profit or Loss for the Period, Fundamental Errors and Changes in Accounting Policies
definition: Guidance on reporting period profit, fundamental errors and policy changes.
example: The standard addressed net profit and changes in accounting policies.

definition: The estimated selling price less the estimated costs of completion and the costs to make the sale.
example: Inventory was written down to net realisable value because it had become obsolete.

definition: Fair value less costs to sell an asset.
example: The net selling price was lower than the asset's carrying amount.

definition: Settlement of a contract by paying or receiving only the net gain or loss.
example: The derivatives allowed net settlement without physical delivery.

definition: Freedom from bias in financial information.
example: Neutrality supports faithful representation of the results.

definition: An asset recently obtained.
example: A newly acquired asset is measured at fair value at acquisition.

definition: The parent entity that is next in the group hierarchy above a lower level parent.
example: The next most senior parent is required to prepare consolidated financial statements that include the whole group.

term: Non- adjusting event [after the balance sheet date]
definition: An event after the reporting date not requiring adjustment.
example: A decline in market value after year-end is a non-adjusting event.

term: Non-adjusting event after the reporting period
definition: Event after period-end that does not change reported figures.
example: A fire after year-end is a non-adjusting event after the reporting period.

definition: A financial institution that is not a licensed bank.
example: The lessor is a non-bank financial service firm.

definition: A lease that cannot be terminated by the lessee without incurring a penalty.
example: The minimum lease payments under the non-cancellable lease were discounted to present value.

definition: Assets other than cash and cash equivalents.
example: Non-cash assets were contributed to the joint venture.

definition: Assets other than cash pledged as security for an obligation.
example: Non-cash collateral must be measured at fair value.

definition: Income or expenses not involving cash movements.
example: Depreciation is a non-cash item added back in the cash flow statement.

definition: Transactions that do not involve cash movements.
example: Non-cash transactions are excluded from the cash flow statement.

definition: The equity in a subsidiary not attributable, directly or indirectly, to a parent.
example: Non-controlling interests are presented separately within equity in the consolidated financial statements.

definition: Equity in a subsidiary not owned by the parent.
example: Non-controlling interests are presented within equity.

definition: Different reporting period ends within a group.
example: Non-coterminous year-ends require adjusting for significant transactions.

definition: Assets expected to be realised beyond twelve months.
example: Non-current assets include property, plant and equipment.

term: Non-current assets (or disposal groups) as held for distribution to owners
definition: Assets expected to be distributed to owners in their capacity as owners rather than sold.
example: The subsidiary's assets were classified as non-current assets held for distribution to owners.

term: Non-current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations
definition: Classification and presentation of assets held for sale and discontinued operations.
example: Non-current assets held for sale are measured at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell.

definition: Obligations expected to be settled after more than twelve months.
example: Non-current liabilities are presented separately from current ones.

definition: Assets not subject to depreciation, such as land.
example: Land is a non-depreciable asset.

definition: An instrument that is not a derivative.
example: A non-derivative contract is classified separately.

definition: A contract whose value does not depend on an underlying variable in the manner of a derivative instrument.
example: The ordinary share purchase contract is a non-derivative contract classified as an equity instrument.

definition: Not subject to discretion.
example: The levy is a non-discretionary payment.

definition: Plan requiring fixed contributions regardless of management choice.
example: The non-discretionary plan obliges the firm to pay bonuses.

definition: Assets such as inventory and equipment rather than financial instruments.
example: Inventory is a non-financial asset.

definition: Effects in a sensitivity analysis where a change in one variable does not produce a proportional change in the outcome.
example: The sensitivity analysis disclosed non-linearities in the relationship between the variables.

definition: Securities that are not traded on an active market.
example: Non-marketable securities are valued using valuation techniques.

definition: An asset not representing a fixed or determinable amount of money.
example: Property, plant and equipment is a non-monetary asset.

definition: Grants received as assets rather than cash.
example: Non-monetary government grants are measured at fair value.

definition: Changes in equity from transactions other than with owners.
example: Comprehensive income reflects non-owner changes in equity.

definition: Ordinary shares that do not give the holder the right to require the issuer to repurchase them for cash.
example: Non-puttable ordinary shares are classified as equity because the holder cannot require redemption.

definition: Distributions made without receiving consideration.
example: Non-reciprocal distributions of assets reduce equity.

definition: Not subject to repayment or redemption by the holder.
example: The preference shares are non-redeemable.

definition: Taxes on purchases that cannot be recovered from tax authorities.
example: Non-refundable purchase taxes form part of the asset's cost.

definition: The production level the facility is expected to achieve on average over a number of periods.
example: Fixed overheads were allocated based on the normal capacity of the production facilities.

definition: Entities whose objective is not to generate profit for owners.
example: Not-for-profit organizations report on their service performance.

definition: Written promises to pay a sum of money at a future date.
example: The entity signed a note payable to the bank.

definition: The face amount underlying a derivative contract.
example: The notional amount of the swap was 10 million.

definition: Free from bias; also a goal or aim.
example: The information should be objective and free from bias.

definition: A past event that creates a present legal or constructive obligation for which a provision must be recognised.
example: The environmental damage constituted an obligating event requiring recognition of a provision.

definition: A duty or responsibility to act or pay.
example: A present obligation is required to recognise a provision.

definition: Duties to dismantle assets and restore sites.
example: The company recognised obligations for removal and restoration.

definition: An interest rate directly observable in the market.
example: The observable interest rate was used to discount cash flows.

definition: Markets for which price information is readily available to participants.
example: Fair value was determined from prices in observable markets.

definition: A market interest rate observed for similar instruments.
example: The fair value was estimated using the observed benchmark interest rate.

definition: A quoted price taken directly from an active market.
example: Fair value was based on the observed market price.

definition: Loss of usefulness due to technological or market change.
example: Obsolescence reduced the asset's recoverable amount.

definition: Gaining or losing power over an entity.
example: Losing control results in deconsolidation.

definition: The price at which a party offers to buy or sell a financial instrument or asset.
example: The offer price is used when measuring the fair value of a liability in the principal market.

definition: Presenting an asset and liability net.
example: Financial assets and liabilities are offset when the criteria are met.

definition: Presenting assets and liabilities net in the statements.
example: Offsetting is permitted only when required or allowed.

definition: A method recognising a gain or loss in a single step.
example: The one-step approach simplified the accounting treatment.

definition: A change in the classification of a financial asset that is permitted in only one direction.
example: The standard allowed a one-way reclassification of the instrument out of the trading category.

definition: A contract where unavoidable costs exceed expected economic benefits.
example: A provision is recognized for the onerous contract.

definition: Funding obligations that create a liability because they are burdensome.
example: Onerous minimum funding requirements gave rise to an additional liability.

definition: Continuous right to use an asset or facility.
example: Ongoing access to the infrastructure is provided under the arrangement.

definition: The balance at the beginning of a period.
example: The opening balance agrees with the prior period's closing balance.

definition: The statement of financial position prepared at the date of transition to IFRSs, being the starting point for first-time adoption.
example: The opening IFRS balance sheet was prepared by recognising and measuring all assets and liabilities in accordance with IFRSs.

term: Opening IFRS statement of financial position
definition: The first IFRS balance sheet at transition.
example: The opening IFRS statement of financial position is prepared at the transition date.

definition: Principal revenue-producing activities of the entity.
example: Cash from operating activities remained positive.

definition: The time between acquiring materials and receiving cash from customers.
example: The operating cycle of the retailer is short.

definition: Decisions relating to the day-to-day use of resources in running an entity's business.
example: Operating decisions about the plant are made by the segment's management.

definition: A lease that does not transfer substantially all ownership risks and rewards.
example: Operating lease payments are recognized as an expense on a straight-line basis.

definition: Lease incentives received or receivable under an operating lease.
example: The entity recognized operating lease incentives over the lease term.

definition: Components reported separately based on internal reporting.
example: Operating segments are identified based on the chief operating decision maker's reports.

definition: A party that operates a facility or service.
example: The operator recognises revenue under the concession agreement.

definition: A contract that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a specified price.
example: The holder of the call option may purchase the shares at the agreed exercise price.

definition: A contract granting a right to buy or sell.
example: The option contract gives the holder the right to buy shares.

definition: Model used to estimate the fair value of an option.
example: The entity used an option pricing model to value the share options.

definition: Contracts giving the holder the right to buy shares.
example: The entity issued options, warrants and their equivalents to investors.

definition: The regular business activities of an entity, excluding unusual or non-recurring items.
example: The gain arose from ordinary activities and was included in operating profit.

definition: Normal day-to-day business activities carried out on arm's length terms.
example: The sale was made in the ordinary course of business.

definition: Owners of ordinary shares in an entity.
example: Profits are distributed to ordinary equity holders as dividends.

definition: A basic equity instrument carrying voting rights.
example: Ordinary shares rank after preference shares on liquidation.

definition: The asset before modification or exchange.
example: The original asset's carrying amount affects the exchange.

definition: The amount originally paid to acquire an asset, before any adjustments.
example: The original cost of the building was based on the purchase price plus transaction costs.

definition: A model where assets are held to collect cash flows.
example: Under the originate and hold business model, assets are measured at amortised cost.

definition: Method treating loans the entity originated itself for disclosure purposes.
example: Under the originated loan approach, only loans the bank granted are included.

definition: Loans and receivables created by the entity itself.
example: Originated loans and receivables are measured at amortised cost.

definition: Costs directly attributable to originating a financial instrument, such as a loan.
example: Loan origination costs are amortised over the life of the loan using the effective interest method.

definition: Entity that creates a financial asset by transferring goods or services.
example: The bank was the originator of the financial asset.

definition: Equity items other than share capital and retained earnings.
example: Other components of equity include the revaluation surplus.

definition: Income and expenses not recognised in profit or loss.
example: Actuarial gains are presented in other comprehensive income.

definition: Long-term benefits other than pensions.
example: Other long-term employee benefits require actuarial measurement.

definition: The risk that the fair value or future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market prices other than those arising from interest or currency risk.
example: Other price risk arises from changes in the market price of the equity instruments held.

definition: An option with an unfavourable exercise price.
example: The option is out of the money when the strike exceeds the share price.

definition: Activities to inform and consult stakeholders about a project.
example: The board launched an outreach programme before revising the standard.

definition: An unconditional sale transferring ownership completely and permanently.
example: The asset was transferred through an outright sale.

definition: Agreements under which an entity contracts with a third party to perform activities on its behalf.
example: Under the outsourcing arrangements, the service provider handles the payroll function.

definition: External party performing services previously handled in-house.
example: The outsourcing provider handles our payroll processing.

definition: Market where securities trade directly between parties off exchange.
example: The shares are traded on the over-the-counter market.

definition: Indirect costs of running a business.
example: Production overheads are allocated to inventory.

definition: The risk of an entity's own default.
example: Own credit risk affects the fair value of liabilities.

definition: A holder of an ownership interest in an entity, such as a shareholder.
example: Transactions with owners in their capacity as owners are recorded directly in equity.

definition: Equity changes from transactions with owners.
example: Owner changes in equity include dividends and share issues.

definition: Property held by its owner for operations, not for rental.
example: Owner-occupied property is accounted for under IAS 16.

definition: Holders of instruments classified as equity in the entity.
example: Distributions to owners are recognised directly in equity.

definition: The proportion of an entity's equity held by an investor.
example: The entity acquired a 25% ownership interest in the joint venture.

definition: Residual interest in the assets after deducting all liabilities.
example: Owners' equity increased after the profitable year.

definition: Capital contributed by shareholders in exchange for shares.
example: The company reported paid in capital of one million.

definition: An entity that controls one or more other entities.
example: The parent prepares consolidated financial statements.

definition: A control relationship between entities.
example: The parent-subsidiary relationship triggers consolidation.

definition: The sale of a portion of an entity's interest in a subsidiary or investment without losing control or significant influence.
example: The partial disposal of the subsidiary's shares did not result in a loss of control.

definition: A subsidiary not wholly owned by the parent.
example: A partially-owned subsidiary gives rise to non-controlling interests.

definition: Members entitled to benefits under a pension plan.
example: All participants in the pension plan receive annual statements.

definition: Equity instruments entitled to share in profits.
example: Participating equity instruments receive a share of distributable profits.

definition: A contract in which an entity collects amounts on behalf of third parties and remits them without recognising them as its own revenue.
example: The utility acted as agent under a pass-through arrangement and recorded only the net fee as revenue.

definition: Combination that occurred in an earlier reporting period.
example: The goodwill arose from a past business combination.

definition: Payment not made by its contractual due date.
example: The receivable was past due by thirty days.

definition: An event that has already occurred and creates an obligation.
example: A past event gave rise to a present obligation.

definition: Change in benefit obligation for past service.
example: Past service cost is recognised when the plan is amended.

definition: Amounts owed by an entity to its suppliers or other parties for goods or services received.
example: Trade payables are presented as current liabilities if payable within twelve months.

definition: Retirement income paid to a person.
example: The pension is paid monthly after retirement.

definition: Present obligation to pay future retirement benefits to employees.
example: The company recognised a pension liability in its statement of financial position.

definition: Arrangement providing post-employment benefits to employees.
example: The company operates a defined benefit pension scheme.

definition: A revenue recognition method under which income is recognised according to the stage of completion of a contract.
example: Revenue on the long-term construction contract was recognised using the percentage of completion method.

definition: Degree to which an entity achieves its financial objectives.
example: The company's performance improved in the second quarter.

definition: Extent to which an entity achieves its financial results.
example: Financial performance is measured by profit and returns.

definition: Conditions requiring specified performance for an award to vest.
example: Share awards vest subject to performance conditions.

definition: The period an employee provides service.
example: Benefits accrue over the period of service.

definition: An annuity that guarantees payments for a fixed number of periods, regardless of whether the recipient survives.
example: A period-certain annuity was purchased to provide income for a fixed ten-year term.

definition: Effects limited to a specific period.
example: Period-specific effects are not extrapolated to other periods.

definition: Debt instruments with no fixed maturity date.
example: Perpetual debt instruments pay interest indefinitely but never repay principal.

definition: Bonus paid for policy renewals or continued participation.
example: Policyholders received a persistency bonus for renewing their contracts.

definition: The employees of an entity, whose costs and benefits are recognised in the financial statements.
example: Personnel costs increased as the company expanded its workforce.

definition: Cash-settled awards valued by reference to the share price.
example: Phantom shares give employees a cash bonus tied to share price.

definition: Capital viewed as the physical productive capacity of an entity.
example: Physical capital is measured in units of production capacity.

term: Plan assets (of an employee benefit plan)
definition: Assets held by a fund to meet employee benefit obligations.
example: Plan assets are measured at fair value at the reporting date.

definition: The date on which a plan is committed.
example: The plan commitment date determines the accounting.

term: Plan to sell the controlling interest in a subsidiary
definition: A formal plan to dispose of a controlling interest in a subsidiary, which may trigger classification as held for sale.
example: A plan to sell the controlling interest in a subsidiary requires the assets to be presented as held for sale.

definition: Provided as security for a loan.
example: The building was pledged as collateral for the loan.

definition: Person or entity that holds an insurance contract.
example: The policyholder may surrender the contract at any time.

definition: Old method combining entities without recognising goodwill.
example: The pooling of interest method was applied to the business combination.

definition: A group of financial assets or liabilities managed together to achieve a common objective.
example: The derivatives are managed as part of a portfolio of interest rate exposures.

term: Portfolio Hedge of Interest Rate Risk
definition: Hedge of interest rate risk on a portfolio of items.
example: The bank applied a portfolio hedge of interest rate risk.

definition: Transfer of a group of insurance contracts or assets.
example: The insurer completed a portfolio transfer of its policies.

definition: Plans providing benefits after employment ends.
example: Post-employment benefit plans are classified as defined contribution or defined benefit.

definition: Benefits payable after employment ends.
example: Post-employment benefits include pensions and lump sums.

definition: The profit or loss of an entity after deducting income tax expense.
example: Profit or loss from discontinued operations is presented on a post-tax basis.

definition: A restriction on transferring shares after vesting.
example: The post-vesting transfer restriction affects the option's fair value.

definition: Instrument that may entitle its holder to ordinary shares.
example: Convertible bonds are potential ordinary shares in diluted EPS.

definition: Rights to obtain voting power if currently exercisable.
example: Potential voting rights are considered when assessing control.

term: Practical ability to sell the asset
definition: The capacity of an entity to dispose of an asset in its present condition without undue delay.
example: Classification as held for sale required the entity to have the practical ability to sell the asset.

definition: Period or amounts existing before the business combination date.
example: Pre-combination revenues were restated in the consolidated accounts.

term: Preface to International Financial Reporting Interpretations Committee
definition: Introductory document explaining the Interpretations Committee's role and authority.
example: The preface describes the Interpretations Committee's objectives.

term: Preface to International Financial Reporting Standards
definition: Introductory document setting out the purpose of IFRS.
